chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The proper way regarding this narration is that we carry it upon one whose habit is killing slaves, because whoever is like that, it is permissible for the Imam to kill him for that, so that others may be deterred from the like of it. But if that occurred from him only exceptionally and rarely, then no more than the slave's price is due from him, according to what we have already stated, along with disciplinary punishment. That which indicates this is what he narrated:

As for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, from 'Ali عليه السلام:
"That he killed a free man for a slave whom he had killed deliberately." He said:

key_terms.ثَمَنِهِ: the monetary value or price of the slave
key_terms.عَادَتُهُ: his established habit or repeated practice
key_terms.يُقْتُلَهُ: to execute him in legal retaliation or punishment
key_terms.ٱلْإِمَامِ: the legitimate authority who may impose such punishment
key_terms.ٱلْوَجْهُ: the proper interpretive approach to the narration

ai.seo_question: When can a free man be executed for killing a slave in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This passage presents a juristic reconciliation of a report stating that Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali عليه السلام executed a free man for intentionally killing a slave. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan explains that this is to be understood in the case of someone known for habitually killing slaves, where the Imam may impose execution as a deterrent; otherwise, the liability is the slave's price together with disciplinary punishment.
